uncited: *   **Inputs:** A dataset of rays $\mathcal{D}$, a neural field model with parameters $\Theta$, hyperparameters $M$ (number of stochastic patches), $K$ (kernel size), $s$ (stride), and $\lambda$ (loss weight).

Where $\SSSIM$ is the average SSIM over $M$ stochastic patches, $\hat{\mathcal{C}}$ are rendered pixels, $\mathcal{C}$ are ground-truth pixels, and $\Patch^{(m)}$ generates the $m$-th stochastic patch.
Default value is 10 to reduce stochasticity, but $M=1$ produces nearly the same good results.
The core loss metric used in this method.

It differs from standard SSIM by averaging SSIM over $M$ stochastic patches rather than local fixed patches, allowing it to capture non-local structural information. [Link](10895-s3im-stochastic-structural-similarity.md)

A neural surface representation method where the multiplex training via S3IM is specifically adapted by replacing the color loss with the multiplex color loss $L_{\mathrm{M},\mathrm{color}}$. [Link](10895-s3im-stochastic-structural-similarity.md) (Contextual link to application)
It was developed to address the limitations of standard SSIM optimization in neural field reconstruction.
